thread.title: What the path to an ‘honest-to-God vicious selloff’ by year end could look like - MarketWatch

author: Shawn Langlois
title: What the path to an ‘honest-to-God vicious selloff’ by year end could look like - MarketWatch
text:
The stock market is coming off a rather limp rebound last week, as the S&P 500 SPX, +0.75% clawed back just a chunk of the prior week’s losses. Keeping the move in check, Apple’s AAPL, -3.04% disappointing report and hand-wringing over U.S.-China trade created more questions than they answered. Toss midterms in the mix and this week has all the makings of another spike in volatility VIX, +2.10% — one that could persist at least through the end of the year.
If the Slope of Hope blog’s Tim Knight has it right, the holiday stretch could be disastrous for those planning to keep their stockings stuffed with equities.
Knight is still basking in the glow of a month in which he logged a 27.7% gain. Not bad considering just how abysmal October was for the bulls. Sometimes it pays to be bearish, though that’s been a tough road over much of the past decade.
‘Maybe there will be a severe political crisis. Maybe the debt choking the planet will finally start to matter. Whatever it is, an honest-to-God vicious selloff will begin, dwarfing what was seen in the autumn.’ Tim Knight Anyway, Knight, who has used his technical approach to navigating the stock market to nail some pretty strong calls lately, came out over the weekend with a detailed scenario for the rest of the year that earns our call of the day .
By the time it’s all over, there will be carnage if it plays out the way he sees it.
“Now, at this point, all of you ‘the future is impossible to predict’ crowd should probably leave, since there’s not much point in reading this,” he wrote in his blog. “But for the rest of you, allow me the opportunity to describe a pathway which we can at least agree is possible.”
This is the general idea of what it could look like:
And here’s how Knight describes each of the above arrows:
The resumption : The selling will resume, and with strength, swiftly re-igniting fears that this is something more than what we’ve seen before. How the midterms plays into this is a mystery. Perhaps we’ll sell off really hard for Monday and Tuesday, and the elections will go hugely in Trump’s favor and end the selloff. Or perhaps the election will be a shocker and cause the market to plunge. The relief : Something substantive will come along that gives the market relief. As I just said, perhaps the election will go in such a way as is considered bullish. Or perhaps there really will be a meaningful US/China trade deal. Whatever it is, it’ll cause committed buying again. The doubt : There will be a brief pause in the strength, since there’s been so much selling, and weaker hands will worry that the bounce is already over. The assurance : However, this will soon stabilize, and buying will resume, pushing the market even higher than it did the first week of November. “The worst is over” crowd will begin to seem truly credible, and people will look forward to a resumption of a confident bull market in 2019. The plunge : Just when things seem calm and the VIX is back in the teens, all holy hell will break loose. Maybe there will be a severe political crisis. Maybe the debt choking the planet will finally start to matter. Whatever it is, an honest-to-God vicious selloff will begin, dwarfing what was seen in the autumn.
We’ll check back in when the ball drops on 2018 to see just how prescient Knight’s bummer of a prediction turns out to be, but for now, with the market mixed to start the week, it’s pretty much anyone’s guess.

The market The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.90% is up just slightly to start what promises to be a choppy week, while the Nasdaq Composite COMP, -0.20% and the S&P 500 SPX, +0.75% are both drifting fractionally lower. Gold GCZ8, -0.19% is up a bit, as is crude CLZ8, -0.44%
Overseas, Asia market s ADOW, -1.33% got knocked around, led by the Hang Seng HSI, -2.08% and the Nikkei NIK, -1.55% . Europe SXXP, -0.16% isn’t showing much conviction in either direction.
The buzz Word from Amazon AMZN, -1.97% on its new headquarters could be coming any day now. The company is reportedly in the advanced stages of selecting a spot in Northern Virginia, which is strategically located just south of the nation’s capital. CEO Jeff Bezos told a conference crowd last week the decision will ultimately come down to “intuition” after all of the data has been considered.
Read: Amazon exec lectures leaker over HQ2
Elon Musk said in an interview last week that Tesla TSLA, -1.13% is not “staring death in the face” and will likely be cash-flow positive for all quarters going forward, meaning the company, for now, doesn’t need more investment for now. Musk also said he is back at a “manageable” 80-hour, 90-hour workweek at Tesla and, the auto maker is “over the hump” with the Model 3 production.
Read: Elon Musk shows off Boring Co. tunnel
The chart Is the historic outperformance of stocks over bonds greatly exaggerated? Jason Zweig of the Wall Street Journal recently tackled that question and came up with some interesting conclusions .
“Maybe investors should question the dogma of ‘stocks for the long run,’” he wrote. “History shows that a portfolio of bonds has outperformed stocks surprisingly often and for shockingly long periods.”
Here’s a chart that goes way, way back:
Zweig explained that the popular belief that there’s never been a 30-year period in which stocks had lower returns than bonds is false. In fact, as recently as 2011, bonds earned higher returns than stocks over the prior 30 years, he said.
The Quote: “I don’t think he’s either capable or willing to change. Instead of talking to the current occupant of that office, I am talking to the American people. I’m saying, you are the ultimate check and balance. It is up to us. As I said in my piece, we cannot wait for someone to rescue us, we must do it ourselves. Everyone, everywhere, must vote in massive numbers” — Captain “Sully” Sullenberger, a lifelong Republican who’s no fan of the current president, in an interview on MSNBC on Saturday .
The stat Getty Images $928 million — That’s how much of its own stock Berkshire Hathaway BRK.A, +5.70% repurchased in the third quarter , a rare move that suggests Chairman Warren Buffett, with a growing cash pile to throw around, is bullish about his company’s investment options.
Read: If you’re expecting buybacks to save this market, don’t
The economy With all the attention on the midterms, there’s not a whole lot to get excited about in terms of economic data. The FOMC is meeting on Wednesday and Thursday, so there’s that. But, of course, no change in policy is expected. Otherwise, as for what’s on tap Monday, we’ll get the ISM nonmanufacturing index at 10:00 a.m. Eastern.
